title: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN lacks D1:Edit, blocking migrations in CI
description: First real migration run (run 31210455090) failed: 'A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/***/d1/database/ff3a01c8-aedb-4bc2-8231-b8511b353728/query) failed. The given account is not valid or is not authorized to access this service [code: 7403]'. The token authenticates and resolves the account fine - every wrangler deploy has worked, including ones that bind D1 - but binding a database only needs Workers Scripts:Edit, while executing SQL against it needs D1:Edit. FIX (Cloudflare dashboard, human only): My Profile > API Tokens > edit the token behind the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN repo secret > add Account > D1 > Edit > save. If the token is scoped to specific accounts confirm it covers the account owning onlooker-db and onlooker-db-staging. No code change can work around this. Blocks onlooker-bw5.
close_reason: Resolved end-to-end in run 31210455090 attempt 3. Token gained D1:Edit; stale staging tables (0 rows) dropped and rebuilt by the migration. Staging now has users/sessions/verification_tokens plus all 9 indexes, and the real queries.ts session lookup runs against it. Production migrated cleanly with its 1 user and 2 sessions intact and d1_migrations now recording 0001_init.sql. All four endpoints return 200, including api-staging.onlooker.dev which never resolved before.

description: Make deploys self-sufficient. title: Staging D1 schema is stale and predates the current API
description: CORRECTION: the original premise was wrong. Cloudflare's d1_databases_list reports num_tables=0 for both databases, but that metadata is stale - direct queries show both are populated. Production (5473b131) holds 1 user and 2 sessions and its schema MATCHES the deployed API: sessions.token_hash and users.name both present, verification_tokens exact. Production auth works; the earlier claim that it could not is retracted. The real fault is staging (ff3a01c8), which carries an older schema from a different era: sessions has token/refresh_token/refresh_expires_at and NO token_hash, users has first_name/last_name and no name, plus a stray audit_logs table from the drizzle schema. That is why 0001_init.sql fails at line 52, CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_token_hash ON sessions(token_hash) - the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS above it is a no-op against the pre-existing table. Staging holds ZERO rows in every table, so dropping and rebuilding is lossless. d1_migrations is empty in staging and absent entirely in production, so these tables were never created through the migration system.
notes: Migration verified safe against production: all three CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS are no-ops, and every one of the 9 indexes targets a column production already has. Applying it there would only record 0001_init as applied.
close_reason: Resolved end-to-end in run 31210455090 attempt 3. Token gained D1:Edit; stale staging tables (0 rows) dropped and rebuilt by the migration. Staging now has users/sessions/verification_tokens plus all 9 indexes, and the real queries.ts session lookup runs against it. Production migrated cleanly with its 1 user and 2 sessions intact and d1_migrations now recording 0001_init.sql. All four endpoints return 200, including api-staging.onlooker.dev which never resolved before.

title: CI deploy jobs invoke pnpm builtin deploy instead of wrangler
description: Deploy steps run 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api deploy --env production'. 'deploy' is a pnpm BUILTIN command (deploys a workspace package to a directory), so it shadows the package script and pnpm rejects --env: [ERROR] Unknown option: 'env'. This is why the post-merge push run on main fails at Deploy to Production even though quality and test now pass. Compounding it, apps/web has no deploy script at all, so even 'pnpm run deploy' would fail there. Root package.json already defines the correct form: deploy:api:prod = 'pnpm --filter @onlooker/api exec wrangler deploy --env production'. Verified both api and web with 'wrangler deploy --env production --dry-run'.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deploy-wrangler-invocation: deploy steps now call the root deploy:api:prod / deploy:web:prod scripts, which use 'exec wrangler deploy --env <env>'. All four commands verified with --dry-run.

title: Test runner broken: vitest 4.1.9 imports vite/module-runner, absent in Vite 5.4.21
description: Monorepo-wide: 'pnpm test' (vitest run) fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED because vitest 4.1.9 imports 'vite/module-runner', which Vite 5.4.21 does not export. No package's *.test.ts files can execute under the runner. Impact: blocks the 'all tests pass' acceptance criterion across the repo (auth-react jwt/schedule tests, web client tests, WS2/WS4 suites). WS3 logic was validated via a standalone Node harness (pure functions) + Playwright E2E as a workaround, but the runner itself must be fixed. Resolution options (all involve a version change, so needs explicit owner sign-off per no-unilateral-bump policy): (a) downgrade vitest to a Vite-5.4-compatible line (e.g. 2.x), (b) upgrade Vite to a line that exports module-runner (6.x/7.x) and revalidate all vite configs, or (c) pin a compatible pair. Recommend the team lead choose the target versions before anyone bumps.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm test runs the full suite without ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED; auth-react jwt/schedule tests execute and pass under the runner
close_reason: Closed

title: WS3: wire reactive terminal-401 to local session reset
description: A mid-session request whose token refresh fails is a terminal 401. WS1 added setUnauthorizedHandler() in api/client.ts; WS3 owns the session-lifecycle half. Expose auth.expireSession() (local-only performLogout, callApi:false) from the auth-react factory and register it via setUnauthorizedHandler in auth.ts so RequireAuth redirects to /login. Must avoid the loop: never call auth.logout() (which POSTs /auth/logout -> 401 -> re-enters handler).
notes: Implemented: factory exposes auth.expireSession() bridged via factory-scope requestLocalLogout ref, populated by a provider effect; auth.ts registers setUnauthorizedHandler(() => auth.expireSession()). All gates pass: auth-react+web typecheck+build. Local-only (callApi:false) avoids /auth/logout loop.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end. auth.expireSession() bridge + setUnauthorizedHandler wiring in auth.ts. Browser test (Playwright): terminal 401 on client-side nav redirects to /login, clears both tokens, no loop, no credential leak. Gates: auth-react+web typecheck+build all pass.

title: applies_to.versions={} conflates version-independent with inference failure
description: ZAppliesTo accepts an empty versions map. That makes 'this lesson genuinely does not depend on a version' indistinguishable from 'the Haiku transform failed to infer versions', and the spec itself notes applies_to cannot be reliably inferred from an artifact. A lesson with versions={} never expires structurally, which is the one guarantee the whole contract rests on - so an inference failure silently produces an immortal lesson. Found by the final whole-branch review of the lesson contract. Disposition: not a contract bug, since the schema cannot tell the two cases apart. The transform (subsystem 2, promotion pipeline) must either always emit at least one version constraint or explicitly mark a lesson version-independent. Decide there, then reflect it in the spec.
design: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md Section 1. Chose option (a) hardened: applies_to.versions is replaced by applies_to.scope, a discriminated union on kind. Branch 'versioned' requires a non-empty versions map; branch 'version_independent' requires a written justification that the tribunal scores via the scope_accuracy criterion. Inference failure can no longer produce a valid lesson - it fails schema validation. Non-emptiness is enforced twice because neither mechanism alone suffices: .check() covers runtime (zod refinements are dropped by z.toJSONSchema) and .meta({minProperties:1}) covers the emitted artifact (.meta does NOT affect runtime validation). Verified in zod 4.4.3. Record kept over array-of-pairs so keys stay unique by construction. Costs schema_version 2.

title: apps/web ignores the brand established in apps/website
description: The product UI shares no visual language with the marketing site. apps/website/src/styles/globals.css defines a real identity - 258 lines with tokens: --bg #080c10, --accent #00d4aa, --sans Syne, --mono DM Mono, dark terminal aesthetic. apps/web uses NONE of it: zero CSS files, zero className usage, no styling dependency, no font declaration at all (so browser default serif), and 71 inline style={{}} objects across 9 pages. Its palette is default framework colors - #007bff (bootstrap blue), #d93025/#188038 (material red/green), #666/#ccc grays. The brand accent #00d4aa appears nowhere in the product. Work: decide the styling mechanism (plain CSS + custom properties reusing the website tokens, vs a framework), extract the shared tokens somewhere both apps can consume, and restyle the 9 auth/dashboard pages. Landing page already proves the aesthetic works, so this is adoption rather than design from scratch.
design: Prefer lifting the existing globals.css tokens into a shared package over inventing a new system - the visual decisions are already made and shipped on the marketing site. Subsystem 6 in the shared lesson contract spec.

title: packages/db drizzle schema and apps/api raw SQL have drifted apart
description: apps/api does not depend on @onlooker/db - it hand-writes SQL in src/db/queries.ts against a 3-table schema (users, sessions with token_hash, verification_tokens) defined in apps/api/migrations/0001_init.sql. packages/db/src/schema.ts defines a different 7-table drizzle schema (adds password_reset_tokens, email_change_tokens, machine_tokens, audit_logs) whose sessions table uses 'token' not 'token_hash'. packages/db has tests that pass against its own schema, so both look healthy in isolation while describing incompatible databases. PR #7 pinned migrations_dir to apps/api/migrations so deploys cannot pick the wrong one, but the underlying divergence remains: features written against packages/db will not work, and the extra 4 tables exist nowhere real. Decide on one source of truth.

title: Design: Shared Lesson contract for cross-machine Playbooks
description: Design spec for the atom of Shared Playbooks. Decisions locked in brainstorming: (1) hosted app exists for cross-person lesson sharing; (2) lessons are the unit, Playbooks are saved-query views; (3) retrieval is tiered — cheap always-on plus deep on demand (Waypoint); (4) promotion gated by tribunal-style N-agent consensus; (5) private/org/public visibility in one pool from the start; (6) contract shape B — claim + evidence + applicability, with a reserved status field so lifecycle is additive. Driving constraint: a real archivist artifact in this repo (vitest/vite mismatch) is now false and would mislead if shared, so staleness must be structural rather than a later phase. Scope is the contract only; retrieval engine, sync API, web app, and visual system are separate sub-projects.
design: Shape B: normative claim + evidence receipts + applicability conditions. Version-scoped applicability lets lessons expire by construction rather than by review.
notes: Spec COMPLETE 2026-08-07 - all five sections approved. Section 3: author_key = HMAC(user_secret, scope) so org and public identities are unlinkable; visibility moves up only, downward is retraction; org keeps custody when a member leaves; public needs a safety/disclosure lens distinct from correctness because correctness rots and harm does not. Section 4: expiry is NOT a status (applies_to just stops matching, no sweep job); contradiction is a signal that triggers tribunal re-judgment, never an automatic verdict; supersession detected by existing Jaccard step, confirmed by consensus; nothing is ever deleted. Section 5: plugins are shell-based in a SEPARATE repo, so the producing side cannot import zod - zod is source of truth, z.toJSONSchema emits the published artifact, apps/api sync endpoint is the enforcement boundary; server accepts schema_version N and N-1 because the two sides cannot upgrade atomically; dedicated packages/lesson-contract chosen over @onlooker/types to avoid inheriting node-html-parser. Next step is writing-plans, not implementation. Known open number: counter-observation threshold in Section 4.

title: Create Deployment Status step fails on every production deploy
description: The final step of deploy-production calls github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus with deployment_id: context.payload.deployment.id. The workflow triggers on push, and push event payloads have no 'deployment' key — that field only exists on deployment/deployment_status events. Result: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id'), so the job reports failure even though both wrangler deploys succeeded (onlooker-api-production 725e1537, onlooker-web-production 7e9db277). Cosmetic but persistent: it will fail on every deploy and masks whether a real deploy problem occurred. The step is redundant anyway — GitHub already records deployments via the job's environment: block.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deployment-status-step: removed the redundant Create Deployment Status step. GitHub already records the deployment via the job's environment: block, so nothing is lost.

title: pnpm lint fails: @onlooker/db cannot resolve @onlooker/config-biome

Pre-existing (reproduced with all working changes stashed). CI does not catch it because the quality job only lints @onlooker/api and @onlooker/web, so root 'pnpm lint' is red while CI stays green.
close_reason: Root cause was not the stated missing devDependency - @onlooker/config-biome was declared and symlinked correctly. packages/db/biome.json extended the bare package name, which has no main/exports, so it resolved to a directory without an index. Changed it to extend @onlooker/config-biome/library.json with root:false, matching every other package. That surfaced 3 pre-existing biome errors in db (never linted before), fixed mechanically with biome check --write.

title: Add hook-layer test for useAuthenticatedFetch terminal-401 surfacing
description: Companion to onlooker-rno (WS1, transport+mock layer). Clean boundary, zero overlap: onlooker-rno proves the transport EMITS exactly one terminal signal (single /auth/refresh coalesce, single onUnauthorized on refresh-of-refresh failure, no retry loop) by testing client.ts + mockApi.ts directly with no React. THIS bead proves the HOOK faithfully SURFACES that one signal. Covers apps/web/src/hooks/useAuthenticatedFetch.ts. Approach: mount the hook (React test renderer / @testing-library/react-hooks equivalent) and mock the apiClient.request boundary so the transport is stubbed — the hook must not add retry/refresh of its own (that lives in the transport). Blocked on the web vitest runner (onlooker-sju).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Happy path: hook goes loading:true -> data set, loading:false, error:null; apiClient.request called exactly once. 2) Terminal 401: request rejects once with AuthApiError(401,'Session expired'); hook exposes error==='Session expired' exactly once, loading:false, data:null, and request is called EXACTLY ONCE (no hook-level retry — the single terminal signal is surfaced, not duplicated or swallowed). 3) Non-401 error (e.g. 500 after transport retries exhausted): surfaced as error string once; hook does NOT call auth.refresh() or clear session (that is transport/WS3's concern, not the hook's). 4) refetch(): re-issues the request, clears prior error, returns to loading:true. 5) skip:true issues no request (loading:false, no call). 6) Unmount mid-flight: no state update after unmount (active-flag guard; no act/setState-after-unmount warning). Suite green under the fixed runner.
notes: Sibling to onlooker-rno per WS1 boundary agreement: rno=transport emits one signal, this=hook surfaces one signal. WS4 owns these acceptance criteria (own hook surface). File now, runs when onlooker-sju (runner fix) lands.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add apps/web tests for JWT/exp mock + refresh transport (blocked on runner)
description: WS1 (Real API Integration) added behavior to apps/web that currently has no automated coverage because the web vitest runner is broken (onlooker-sju). Once the runner works, cover: (1) mock issues JWT-shaped access/refresh tokens with real exp; getTokenExpiration parses exp from the payload. (2) exp enforcement: expired access -> 401 on /auth/me; expired refresh -> 401 on /auth/refresh. (3) hybrid validation: in-session owner-map is authoritative (rotation/logout/email-rename); stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp fallback validates a still-valid token after the owner map is cold (reload safety). (4) revocation: invalidateSessions / logout add tokens to REVOKED_TOKENS and subsequent use 401s. (5) transport single-flight refresh: one 401 storm coalesces into a single /auth/refresh, then replays; refresh-of-refresh failure surfaces the terminal 401 and fires onUnauthorized exactly once (no retry loop). Files: apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts, apps/web/src/api/client.ts.
acceptance_criteria: Vitest suite in apps/web covering exp enforcement, hybrid/reload validation, revocation, and single-flight refresh+terminal-401; green under the fixed runner.

title: WS1: mock issues exp-bearing JWTs + stateless validation (reload-safe, activates refresh/expiry)
description: WS3 flagged two mock gaps blocking their acceptance criteria: (1) module-level token Maps are per-realm, so after a page reload GET /auth/me 401s a token still in localStorage -> session does not persist on reload; (2) opaque mock-access-* tokens have no exp, so proactive auto-refresh + expiry warning stay dormant. Fix in apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts: issueTokens mints real JWTs with exp (access short, refresh long); token->email resolution becomes hybrid — in-memory Maps stay authoritative in-session (preserves rotation/logout/WS2 email-rename), falling back to stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp check when Maps are cold (post-reload) so a seeded session survives reload. Enforce exp so reactive refresh-on-401 fires. Revoke superseded tokens on rotation/logout. No signature changes to emailFromAuthHeader/requireAuth so WS2/WS4 handlers are unaffected.
close_reason: Implemented in apps/web/src/api/mockApi.ts: issueTokens now mints exp-bearing JWTs (access 15min, refresh 30d) via mintJwt+base64UrlEncode; token->email resolution is hybrid (in-memory Maps authoritative in-session, stateless decodeJwtPayload+exp fallback when cold/post-reload); exp enforced so reactive refresh-on-401 fires; superseded/logged-out tokens revoked. emailFromAuthHeader/requireAuth signatures unchanged (WS2/WS4 untouched). Verified: encode<->decode round-trip against auth-react decoder (11/11 checks incl UTF-8, exp, opaque->null); typecheck/lint/build green. Browser demo (reload persistence + expiry warning firing) handed to WS3 to confirm.

Add a runtime setUnauthorizedHandler seam on api/client.ts and wire the singleton's onUnauthorized to delegate to it, so WS3 (session lifecycle) can register a LOCAL-only session reset without a network re-trigger loop. Also fold WS4's GET /api/users/me and GET /api/dashboard into the api/types.ts endpoint contract doc.

title: WS2: Email verification check + resend flow
Revisit author_key width once HMAC derivation is implemented
description: The lesson contract pins author_key to 12 lowercase hex characters, matching ZProjectKey. That is a truncated HMAC: 48 bits, so collision resistance is weak at scale (birthday bound around 16M identities per scope) even though unlinkability is unaffected by truncation. Section 3 of the spec defines author_key = HMAC(user_secret, scope). When subsystem 2 actually derives these keys, confirm 12 hex is wide enough for the expected identity count per scope, or widen the contract and bump schema_version. Raised while applying final-review fixes; the 12-hex choice was taken deliberately for consistency with project_key and because existing fixtures use it.
design: RESOLVED 2026-08-08 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-promotion-pipeline-design.md Section 1. ZAuthorKey widens from 12 to 32 lowercase hex (48 -> 128 bits). ZProjectKey stays at 12: it is a local-only opaque label with no security role, and the two were only ever coupled by convention. Rationale: Section 3 of the contract spec gives author_key two collision-sensitive jobs, org revocation and public blocking, where a collision blocks an innocent author alongside a bad actor. Rides along free on the schema_version 2 bump that onlooker-7jn already forces.

title: api-staging.onlooker.dev does not resolve
description: Checked all four deploy domains: app.onlooker.dev 200, api.onlooker.dev 200, app-staging.onlooker.dev 200, but api-staging.onlooker.dev fails to connect (curl exit, no HTTP status). wrangler.toml [env.staging] routes the API to api-staging.onlooker.dev/*, so either the staging API has never been deployed or the DNS record is missing. Staging deploys only run on push to the staging branch, which may never have happened. Not blocking - found while fixing onlooker-g03.
close_reason: Closed

title: @onlooker/types declares entrypoints that do not exist
description: packages/types/package.json sets main='index.ts' and exports {'.': './index.ts', './integration': './integration/index.ts'}, but neither packages/types/index.ts nor packages/types/integration/ exists. The package only ships flat modules (user.ts, common.ts, errors.ts, ...), which resolve through the './*': './*.ts' subpath. Latent, not currently breaking: nothing in apps/ or packages/ imports @onlooker/types at all. Fix by adding a barrel index.ts or dropping the dead export entries.
close_reason: Removed main and the '.' / './integration' export entries; neither packages/types/index.ts nor packages/types/integration/ ever existed. Kept the './*' subpath, which is the only entry that resolved to real files. Verified: @onlooker/types/user and /common resolve to existing files, bare @onlooker/types now resolves to nothing rather than a phantom index.ts. Zero importers repo-wide, so no consumer impact. User chose this over adding a barrel index.ts.

title: Packages ship test files in dist output
description: auth-core, auth-react, db (tsc builds) and cache (vite-plugin-dts) all emit compiled test files into dist/. auth-react ships 12 such files, cache 20, auth-core 3, db 3. Test code should not be part of published package output. packages/logger already solves this with a separate tsconfig.build.json that excludes test globs while tsconfig.json (used by typecheck) still covers them.
close_reason: Fixed in chore/exclude-tests-from-package-builds: tsconfig.build.json for auth-core/auth-react/db (following logger's existing pattern) plus a dts exclude for cache. Verified: cold rebuild emits zero test artifacts, all declared entrypoints intact.

title: Deployment docs still reference onlooker.example.com placeholders
description: Eight tracked docs still document placeholder domains (onlooker.example.com, api.onlooker.example.com) while the apps actually route to app.onlooker.dev / api.onlooker.dev: CLOUDFLARE_SETUP.md, DEPLOYMENT.md, DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md, DEPLOYMENT_README.md, ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md, QUICK_START_DEPLOY.md, apps/api/DEPLOYMENT.md, apps/web/DEPLOYMENT.md. Anyone following them would configure CORS_ORIGIN and VITE_API_URL against domains that do not exist. Note: test fixtures using test@example.com are correct and must NOT be changed - example.com is the reserved domain for exactly that. Split out of onlooker-g03, which covered deploy.yml only.

title: Deploy environment URLs use placeholder example.com domains
description: deploy.yml sets environment.url to https://staging.onlooker.example.com and https://onlooker.example.com, but wrangler.toml routes the apps to app-staging.onlooker.dev and app.onlooker.dev. The deployment links GitHub surfaces in the UI therefore point at domains that do not exist. Cosmetic only, no effect on the deploy itself. Left out of the deploy-invocation fix to keep that PR narrow.
close_reason: Pointed both environment.url values and both Notify Deployment deployment_url constants at the real wrangler routes: app.onlooker.dev (production) and app-staging.onlooker.dev (staging), i.e. the user-facing web app rather than the API. Verified both return HTTP 200 before switching. Workflow YAML re-parsed to confirm both environment blocks are correct.
